one_month_reasoning: Window to 2026-10-31: (1) No Q3 results date is announced; Q2 was Aug 4 and Q3-25 Nov 3, so earnings most likely fall just outside the window. (2) Oct-28 FOMC: Polymarket ($22.1M vol, 2026-10-02) 75% hold / 25% +25bp; a hold is mildly supportive for this levered, rate-sensitive name, a hike a clear negative, with the 10-yr already at 5.24%. (3) The 8-K guides first Barber Lake rent to 'Q4 2026' (not specifically October), so a first-rent release could land in or after the window: expected, small positive. (4) Late-October hyperscaler capex prints drive AI-infrastructure beta both ways. (5) The V3 Oct-23 forward tranche is pre-hedged, not new supply, so I drop the selling-overhang drag I had in round 1; offsetting that, I drop the small reversal tilt. Net: near-symmetric lognormal centered ~$15.4 with ~31% monthly sigma (112%/3.5 = 32%).

bear.story: Barber Lake halls slip or overruns run past the $359.3M layer and need ATM equity; no new lease through 2027 and ERCOT Batch Zero (Apr-2027) disappoints; GPU rents fall as Rubin ships, raising doubts about Fluidstack (only ~45% Google-backstopped) and the unnamed AI-lab follow-on; stock converges on contracted-only value ($5.74 split-rate, $4.18 at a single 9%).

base.story: Black Pearl and Barber Lake fully delivered by Q1-2027, Stingray rent from Apr/May-2027; run-rate NOI near $727M in 2028; one of Odessa/Reveille/Ulysses signs; rates flat. The market values AWS-guaranteed rent at bond-like rates (my split-rate DCF $9.3, NAV $12.2) and pays some pipeline optionality on top.

bull.story: 0.5-1 GW of new hyperscale leases (Colchis/Mikeska/McLennan after Batch Zero, or Odessa/Ulysses) signed at >$1.4M/IT MW with project financing; power scarcity keeps prior-gen GPUs rented; rates ease and the AI-infrastructure trade re-rates toward consensus (~$29).

thesis_break_reason: $7.25 is the split-rate contracted-only DCF ($5.74; $4.18 at a single 9% rate) plus a token ~$0.75B (~$1.5/share) of pipeline. A close there would mean the market is impairing the signed AWS/Fluidstack leases (delivery failure, overruns well beyond $359.3M, Fluidstack stress in a GPU-rent glut, doubt about the AI-lab follow-on, or a forced parent equity raise), not just pricing out the pipeline or ordinary 112%-vol noise.

reasoning: Round 4 (site coverage and split discounting). (1) Rebuilt the DCF by site from the checked inventory instead of the company's aggregate Q2-26 NOI schedule (which predates the Barber Lake re-phasing and AI-lab commitment): Black Pearl ($296M yr-1, to ~2041) and Stingray ($108M, May-2027 to 2042) for AWS with Amazon.com guarantees; Barber Lake Fluidstack years 1-10 ($331M yr-1, ~Jan-2027 to ~2037, ~45% Google-backstopped) and then the unnamed AI lab years 11-20 ($5.2B, to ~2047) -- correcting round 3's inverted tenant order. Site rent sums to ~$714M in 2028 vs the company's $727M, a 2% check. (2) Replaced the 2% Gordon terminal with the supervisor's expiry-based renewal model (75% renew at 85% rent, refit capex, 8.5% aged-shell cap) and cut the follow-on haircut to 10% with no perpetuity carry (removes the double count). (3) Split discounting: AWS term 6.5% and Fluidstack term 7.5%, anchored on the 6.0-6.125% and 7.125% secured notes plus ~40bp; AI-lab term 8.5%; tails, overhead and pipeline at 9%. Single-rate DCF $7.72 (close to round 3's $7.8: the harsher terminal offsets the larger AI-lab rent), split-rate $9.28. (4) Every inventory site now appears once: ten pipeline sites probability-weighted net of $10.5M/IT MW capex and fees ($1.73B, vs a bundled $1.2B), Colchis at 76%, Odessa mining ($0.02B) and Odessa HPC conversion on the same 207 MW without double counting, WindHQ JVs excluded with the Canaan shares (~$0.02B) credited to net debt. NAV rises to $12.2 (pipeline and site caps). Fair value $9.0 -> $10.4. The ladder shifts up ~3% (median ~$13.0 -> ~$13.4, P(>=15.46) 0.417 -> 0.431): the higher value comes from re-rating bond-like rent, which the market may not pay for while the stock trades on lease optionality and sector beta. 1-month ladder unchanged: nothing new in the window. Facts used as given by the inventory; no fact changed, so no new primary-source checks were needed beyond the Canaan quote.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Applies to tenants' GPU revenue, not CIFR's rent: contract price for the contract term; after it ~-50% over ~18-24 months after the next Nvidia generation, then ~-10%/yr, levelling near cost-per-compute parity (~$3/PFLOP-hr), cash tail while rent > power + colo. Reaches CIFR through (a) Fluidstack's first fleet refresh (~2032): 5% EL on unbacked rent; (b) the AI-lab follow-on (2037-47): 10% EL at 5y (5% at 7y, 15% at 4y); (c) renewal at expiry: renewal odds / re-lease rent / refit capex 75%/85%/$2.0M per IT MW at 5y (80%/90%/$1.5M at 7y; 70%/80%/$2.5M at 4y).
gpu_life.note: Powered-shell landlord: tenants own and refresh GPUs; no CIFR GPU capex. Refit capex at lease expiry is consistent with life (shorter life, faster density change, more refit). Base 5y kept: fact-checked company lives are CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5 (since Jan-2026), IREN 5. 4-yr stress $8.45. Single-rate equivalents: 4y $6.90, 5y $7.72, 7y $8.53.

discounting.contracted_rate: 6.5% AWS term (Black Pearl, Stingray); 7.5% Fluidstack term (Barber Lake yrs 1-10); 8.5% AI-lab term (yrs 11-20, plus 10% EL)
discounting.basis: Cipher's secured project notes against each contract: Black Pearl 6.125% and Stingray 6.000% (Ba2/BB-, AWS with Amazon.com AA/A1 guarantee; yields ~5.3% at 6/30/26 quotes of ~103), Cipher Compute 7.125% for Barber Lake (Ba3/BB-, ~6.2% yield). Coupons used as the anchor since the 10-yr has risen to 5.24%; +~40bp for the unlevered residual (operating, completion and refinancing risk beyond the 2030-31 maturities). Fluidstack is unrated with a ~45% Alphabet backstop, so 100bp over AWS, matching the note spread gap. AI lab is unnamed and unrated with no debt priced: 8.5%, between 7.5% and the 9.0% WACC, with a 10% expected-loss haircut for default. Renewal tails, overhead and pipeline at 9.0% WACC.
